profiles.name: Terry Lemond Dorsey
profiles.description: Terry Lemond Dorsey, 21, was charged in Baton Rouge, LA with co-defendants Kenyatta Huggins and Shamyrin Johnson for the May 31 - June 1, 2020 arsons at four area businesses. He admitted to starting the fires; the motive related to anti-police tensions: he said he was "angry about what was going on and wanted to attack who was attacking us." Sentenced to 18 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: WAFB explicitly identifies left portrait as Terry Dorsey and credits East Baton Rouge sheriff. WBRZ thumbnail is three-person composite with banner; not usable unchanged. Original individual source or clean verified crop remains lead.

profiles.name: Thomas Wilder Moseley
profiles.description: Thomas Wilder Moseley, 29, was charged in Minneapolis, MN with possessing firearms and ammunition while being an unlawful user of controlled substances. He resisted arrest after being seen reaching for his waistband, which held a loaded handgun. The protest was held outside the Government Center and was part of the Summer 2020 wave of protests after George Floyd's murder. Sentenced to time served plus 2 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: Hennepin complaint and local FOX9/CBS reporting corroborate case; no separately identified usable portrait extracted. Social crime-watch image needs original provenance.

profiles.name: Timothy James Goodner
profiles.description: Timothy James Goodner, 19, was involved in an act of arson concerning the Shaia's Parking Lot attendant booth on May 30, 2020 as part of the George Floyd protests. Government dismissed the indictment and supplemental information without prejudice.
profiles.finding: DOJ case-list and Cleveland reporting found. Cleveland LinkedIn name/location alone insufficient identity proof; old genealogy namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Tyree Walker
profiles.description: Tyree Walker, 23, was charged in Las Vegas, NV with conspiracy to commit arson and arson with co-defendants Devarian Haynes, 23, and Ricardo Densmore, 24, after they were identified on video (taken by Densmore) of Walker and Haynes setting a police car on fire on May 30, 2020. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Las Vegas co-defendant reporting found; Maryland, Chicago, Arizona and Texas booking namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Victor A. Sanchez-Santa
profiles.description: Victor A. Sanchez-Santa was arrested on June 18, 2020, and charged federally with attempting to set fire to an NYPD vehicle in Manhattan during a George Floyd protest. He appeared by video from a holding cell that day and was released to his mother’s supervision on a $250,000 bond. A grand jury indicted him on September 14. In January 2021 prosecutors placed him in a nine-month deferred-prosecution program with conditions including anger-management treatment, and in November 2021 they dismissed the case because further prosecution was not in the interests of justice. No jail or prison confinement beyond the day of arrest is documented.
profiles.finding: Fox report and deferred-prosecution document corroborate case; no verified real portrait. Guatemala physician and padel namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Alexis Butler
profiles.description: Alexis Butler, 25 at the time and of Dania Beach, Florida, was one of the "GEO9," a group of Fort Lauderdale Food Not Bombs activists arrested for the December 3, 2019 blockade of the Boca Raton, Florida headquarters of the GEO Group — the private-prison corporation that operates immigration detention centers for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, including Florida's Broward Transitional Center. The activists sealed the building's entrances, parking garage and elevators with concrete-filled tires and barrels to shut down "business as usual" and protest GEO's role in immigrant detention and family separation. Initially charged only with misdemeanor trespassing, the protesters were re-arrested in February 2020 on far more serious felony charges — false imprisonment and conspiracy to commit false imprisonment — after police alleged that a security guard had been confined inside the building during the blockade, exposing them to up to 15 years in prison. The escalation was widely criticized, including by U.S. Rep. Ted Deutch, as an attempt to criminalize and chill political protest against the private-prison industry. Butler was arrested at her Dania Beach home and held about four days in the Broward County jail before posting bond.
profiles.finding: Miami Herald and NYCABC corroborate GEO9 identity. Wedding, hockey, basketball, photographer and Chicago housing professional portraits not linked; reject.

profiles.name: Richard Joseph Klimek
profiles.description: Richard Joseph Klimek was one of five men indicted by a Multnomah County grand jury on August 30, 2019, following the August 17 demonstrations and counterdemonstrations in Portland. He was charged with felony riot, attempted third-degree assault, second-degree criminal mischief, unlawful entry into a motor vehicle and first-degree theft. The announcement documents an indictment but does not say that Klimek was arrested, booked or confined, and no custodial disposition has been established.
profiles.finding: MCDA indictment and Willamette Week corroborate case; no verified portrait; cemetery namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Sydney Clifford
profiles.description: Sydney Clifford was one of 22 Greenpeace activists federally charged after the September 12, 2019 blockade of the Houston Ship Channel from the Fred Hartman Bridge, a protest against fossil-fuel exports in which climbers suspended themselves from the span. Held from September 12, they were released on September 14, 2019 when a federal magistrate granted all 22 personal-recognizance bonds. Reported as 21 years old at the time of the arrest, and resident in Portland, Oregon. No one charged received a prison sentence; the state and federal cases were eventually resolved through agreements leading to dismissal.
profiles.finding: Click2Houston case list identifies21-year-old Portland participant; TikTok celebrity born2004 and war memorial namesakes rejected. No individually identified image found.

profiles.name: Chase A. Davis
profiles.description: Chase A. Davis, 21, was arrested in Florida on Mississippi charges alleging he sent Facebook death threats to the American Family Association, an anti-LGBTQ organization. PACER records sealed. 6 months federal prison + 2 years supervised release + $1,440 restitution.
profiles.finding: AFA first-party release corroborates Pompano Beach threats case; no verified portrait located.

profiles.name: Alexander Gorman Dial
profiles.description: Alexander Gorman Dial, 37, indicted Sept 29, 2019 on felony riot, second-degree assault, third-degree assault, and criminal mischief for the Aug 17, 2019 Portland antifa-Proud Boys counter-protest. 6 victims injured. Took plea July 2018 (per source); details data not available.
profiles.finding: MCDA and Willamette Week corroborate2019 defendant; hostile aggregator has image lead but original source and image suitability unverified. Existing biography dates inconsistent; flag separate review.

profiles.name: Suzanne Muscara
profiles.description: Suzanne Muscara, age 37, mailed a threatening letter containing fake anthrax to Republican Senator Susan Collins along with a stick-figure drawing of the senator with X eyes. Convicted at trial; 30 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Bangor Daily News article access unsuccessful; CBS corroborates case. New York coach spouse namesake rejected. No verified portrait.

profiles.name: Francisco Joseph Arcila Ramirez
profiles.description: Francisco Joseph Arcila Ramirez, age 36, an ELN (National Liberation Army) member, supplied weapons shipments to the Colombian terrorist organization. Pleaded guilty in U.S. federal court; 240 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Federal appellate opinion and docket corroborate identity; no usable portrait in returned evidence.

profiles.name: Carlos Bayon
profiles.description: Carlos Bayon was a Grand Island, New York resident arrested on August 1, 2018 after leaving threatening voicemail messages for U.S. Representatives Steve Scalise and Cathy McMorris Rodgers. Bayon said he made the calls to draw attention to the Trump administration's family-separation policy. A federal jury convicted him in August 2019 of two counts of threatening a federal official and two counts of transmitting interstate threats. On November 21, 2019, Judge Lawrence Vilardo sentenced him to concurrent 60-month prison terms followed by one year of supervised release. He was released from federal custody on March 16, 2023.
profiles.finding: Grand Island/Scalise query corroborates case but available article image is Scalise, not Bayon. Argentine disappeared person, researcher, chef and genealogy namesakes excluded.
